verdicts.note: SSRI -> spermatogenesis. Semen parameters, not a fertility outcome.
SSRI use and male infertility, retrospective. Indication design not stated in the abstract.
Harvard Review of Psychiatry review of SSRIs and conception in couples. Channel-1 seed the A3 set did not hold; LEAKAGE WALL applies.
Brief review, both sexes, ability to conceive. Channel-1.
Preprints.org record; version of record must be located before use.
Fecundability persistence within couples. No medication exposure; a fecundability-modelling parameter with no B.7 content.
Pilot, SSRI and male fertility potential. Reverse causation named in the abstract itself (infertility -> stress -> depression).
SR+MA of SSRIs on semen quality. Channel-1 for the mechanism stream; LEAKAGE WALL applies.
Clinical Q&A on SSRIs, sperm, and paternal exposure.
Narrative review, paternal SSRI use. Mixes male fertility with neonatal outcomes; the neonatal half is Wall 4.
Wistar rats. Wall 7.
Switching to vortioxetine to relieve treatment-emergent sexual dysfunction.
Cell-phone exposure and fecundability. Right outcome, wrong determinant.
Citalopram vs agomelatine on sperm parameters; a case report plus review, so n=1 on the causal side.
In vitro human sperm. Human tissue, so not Wall 7, but no fertility outcome.
Long-term side effects incl. sexual dysfunction across agents.
Age, fecundity and fecundability in women. A.15's estimand, no medication.
Sertraline inhibits CatSper Ca2+ channels in human sperm. The sharpest mechanism record in the batch.
Pharmacovigilance signal analysis; ascertainment is spontaneous reporting, which is the low end of the link-1 range.
Mouse germ cells. Wall 7.
Clubfoot. Wall 4.
Review of SSRI reproductive toxicity. Species mix must be separated at full text.
Dose-response for depression remission.
Switching to relieve SSRI-induced sexual dysfunction.
Antidepressants on male reproduction and sexual function.
Double-blind placebo-controlled ejaculation study. Randomised evidence on link 1.
SSRIs and the endocrine system. The endocrine pathway the v5 claim asserts.

KEY RECORD. Urinary SSRI biomarker across pregnancy-establishment windows, prospective cohort, outcomes fecundability AND pregnancy loss. Biomarker exposure sidesteps the prescription-is-not-ingestion problem. Record carries no abstract; likely an ASRM abstract, and the version of record must be located.
In vitro estrogenic activity of SSRI molecules.
Montejo et al. 2001, the direct-questioning incidence study. Recovered here as a frame record because A3 could not key it to a DOI; this is the DOI-less index copy.
Review with an explicit coverage-policy framing.
Head-to-head agent comparison; bupropion as the low-dysfunction comparator.

Self-reported pharmaceutical use and primary OVULATORY infertility, case-control. Female, and a fertility outcome. Predates the SSRI era, so the exposure is largely tricyclic and the record informs the pre-1988 baseline rather than the SDT cell.
Asprosin infusion rescuing SSRI-induced dysfunction; animal model. Wall 7.
Conceptual essay on subfertility with no medication content.
GENDEP, with a measured pre-treatment baseline and a pharmacogenetic moderator.
Within-class tolerability comparison including sexual side effects.
Narrative review; the 'potential solutions' half is OFF_CLINICAL_MANAGEMENT and is separated at full text.
Long-term depression treatment. Useful only for the 1987 market-entry date the timing wall rests on.
Danish nationwide SSRI exposure and miscarriage. Wall 3: B.5's channel, B.7's treatment, no fertility outcome. Cross-file to B.5, no recall credit here.
Second index copy of Montejo et al. 2001; duplicate of W2229937731 and collapses to it at extraction.
Cardiac arrest. Note the case-time-control design, which is the kind of within-person exposure contrast Wall 1 asks for and which nobody has applied to a fertility outcome.
Mechanisms and clinical implications review.
Demographic vs epidemiological approaches to measuring fecundity. Outcome-side measurement rather than exposure-side, and directly load-bearing for the estimand-level distinction.
Herbal remedies for antidepressant-induced infertility.
Nordic four-country SSRI/SNRI utilisation with trends and switching. Directly usable exposure-prevalence series.
Wall 7 — but note the finding runs the other way: in a depressed animal model paroxetine IMPROVED sperm quality, which is Call 2's sign ambiguity observed rather than argued.
Cognition in very old women.
AMH and fecundability. No medication exposure.
Birth defects. Wall 4.
Female sexual side effects, 33 patients, descriptive. Small, and one of few female-specific link-1 records.
Sprague-Dawley rats. Wall 7.
LC-MS/MS assay of psychotropic levels in seminal fluid. An exposure measure that would settle prescription-versus-ingestion if anyone applied it to a fertility outcome.
Montejo et al. 1997, 344 patients, prospective. The precursor to the 2001 study.
Prospective SRI sexual dysfunction study.

KEY RECORD. Major depression AND antidepressant use against male and female fertility in one estimate — the Wall 1 contrast the chapter needs, and the only record so far that names both exposures. Record carries no abstract; version of record must be located.
Panic-disorder treatment comparison.
Female sexual dysfunction on SSRIs with a 5-HT2A polymorphism moderator.
Prescribing phenotype of NaSSA patients.
2025 SR of antidepressants on male fertility and seminal parameters. Channel-1; LEAKAGE WALL applies.
